|strategy=By [mailto:hutsons@t-online.de Larry Hutson]<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/dontdothatagain.html</ref>

How many times have you seen the following: DS player starts with [[Mobilization Points]], deploys [[Raithal]] from his Reserve Deck and drops some character at a docking bay to boost their Force generation on turn 2 by at least 4?

Well, the Jedi's intolerance of silly behavior will soon put an end to that!

First of all, [[Don't Do That Again (Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty){{!}}Don't Do That Again]] meets all the restrictions of [[Heading For The Medical Frigate]], so you can use it as a starting Effect &#150; killing a popular DS strategy from the word go. To counter this card, your opponent will have to field a space presence, but now they'll have to rely on drawing a battleground system and ship normally... they can't pull any of the systems or the [[Executor]] using [[Mobilization Points]]' game text!

The other portion of [[Don't Do That Again (Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty){{!}}Don't Do That Again]]'s game text is no less powerful, letting you pull an Immediate Effect from your Reserve Deck once per game. With a little insight into your opponent's deck, you can rummage through your deck and get just the card you need. Pull [[What Was It?]] for some dueling protection for your Jedi. Pull [[Imperial Atrocity]] to make your opponent reconsider a big, fat Force drain of more than two. Press the [[Advantage]] when you defeat [[Maul]], [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]], Mara, or the Emperor in a battle or duel. Or weaken a [[Jabba]]'s Palace all-alien deck with [[A Gift]] and any old droid. None of those options appeal to you? Then use [[Don't Do That Again (Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty){{!}}Don't Do That Again]] to pull What Are You Tryin' To Push On Us? and grab a recycling Interrupt your opponent's relying on.

Like the card says, the Jedi don't tolerate such silliness for long!

Discourage a key part of your opponent's strategy by countering it. Who knows? He may heed your advice and not do that again!

Force the issue a bit more by making your opponent draw both a battleground system and starship... just be careful of [[Battle Order]]!
